description:
The shared in-process integration harness moves from a per-target `#[path]` include into `jit`'s existing `test-support` library surface, so it compiles once.

## Background

`crates/jit/tests/common/harness.rs` (about 336 lines, `#![allow(dead_code)]` because each includer uses a subset) is pulled in by `#[path = "../common/harness.rs"] mod harness;` in four of the ten integration targets: `fast_docs_templates`, `fast_issue`, `fast_rules` and `cli_query_graph` (which uses only `seed_memory_issue`). Each target recompiles it. Everything it needs is already reachable through the `test-support` feature: `commands::test_helpers::memory_executor`, `test_mode::enable` and the public `InMemoryStorage` constructors. `crates/jit/Cargo.toml` enables `test-support` for every test build through its self dev-dependency, so code gated `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))` is compiled once in the library build that every target links. `dev/TESTING.md` documents the `#[path]` convention.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The harness is a module of the `jit` library gated on `cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))`, beside the existing fixture homes, and carries no blanket `allow(dead_code)`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No integration target declares a `#[path]` include of the harness, `crates/jit/tests/common/` no longer exists, and the four former includers reach the harness through `jit::` paths.
- [hard] REQ-03: The integration-target count is unchanged and the four suites pass with their existing assertions.
- [hard] REQ-04: `dev/TESTING.md` describes the harness at its new library location, with no remaining instruction to `#[path]`-include it.

## Notes

A new `jit-test-support` crate was rejected because it adds a build unit without adding a capability. The build-footprint budgets are re-measured when the epic closes. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.
title: Compile the integration harness once in jit's test-support surface
